questions.explain: The chapter states the autonomous rule: calls_in_window >= 20 AND mean_exec_time > baseline_mean + 3*baseline_stddev AND sustained for two consecutive intervals before confirming a regression.
options: calls_in_window >= 20 AND mean_exec_time > baseline_mean + 3 * baseline_stddev, sustained for at least two consecutive collection intervals
Any single execution slower than 5 seconds
Two consecutive queries with different plan_ids
Any query whose plan changes after an index is created
questions.q: What is the chapter's rule for confirming a plan regression candidate before triggering remediation?

questions.explain: The chapter recommends scheduling re-evaluation every 24 hours: temporarily unforce the plan, observe one collection window, and force again only if the regression persists — preventing stale plan forces from accumulating.
options: Forced plans are permanent and never reviewed
Re-evaluate every 24 hours: temporarily unforce, observe one collection window, and force again only if the regression persists
Unforce the plan immediately after the first successful execution
Forced plans are automatically removed at the next statistics update
questions.q: After forcing a good plan, what feedback loop does the chapter require to avoid accumulating stale plan forces?

questions.explain: The gate checks table size (schedule during maintenance window with ONLINE = ON if > 100 GB), write amplification from sys.dm_db_index_operational_stats, and a redundancy check for existing indexes covering the proposed columns.
options: Verify the index name follows naming conventions
Check table size, estimate write amplification from DML rates, and verify no existing index already covers the proposed columns
Check that the index is non-clustered and under 10 GB
Verify the query text contains a WHERE clause
questions.q: What three safety gates must an index candidate pass before the autonomous system creates it on production?

questions.explain: AUTOPILOT lets the optimizer reason about a hypothetical index that doesn't exist yet — the system requests the estimated plan without executing the query, then rolls back the hypothesis with no write to disk.
options: It creates the index in a test database
It analyzes missing-index DMVs without touching the engine
It builds the index with ONLINE = OFF for speed
It lets the optimizer reason about a hypothetical index that does not yet exist — requesting the estimated plan without executing the query, then rolling back with no disk write
questions.q: What is the purpose of the AUTOPILOT hypothetical-index tool in the chapter's autonomous index validation flow?

questions.explain: The validation loop requires a pre-action baseline, applying the change, observing a post-action window (2-3 collection intervals), and automatically reverting (drop index, unforce plan, remove hint) if metrics are unchanged or worse.
options: Record a pre-action baseline, apply the change, and mark it confirmed immediately
Apply the change and alert the DBA to verify manually
Record a pre-action baseline, apply the change, observe a post-action window, and automatically revert if metrics are unchanged or worse
Apply changes only during maintenance windows
